headline: High-risk shared-filesystem and shell-capable pair: Goose can overwrite or act on workspace content while the other profile is a non-runnable docs-only collection, creating default dangerous interaction and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose reads and writes the user filesystem and uses MCP/extensions, so attacker-controlled files can influence its tool use. The other profile is a docs-only collection with no runnable surface, so direct bidirectional injection is not shown; however, shared workspace content can still be parsed as instructions by Goose.
conditions: IF Goose is pointed at a workspace containing untrusted text files
IF the operator copies Goose output into another agent or parser
mitigations: Restrict Goose to a dedicated empty workspace
Review any file-derived instructions before execution
Use manual copy-paste only for trusted snippets
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for file content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose can read files in cwd and has broad network egress, so sensitive workspace data can leave the machine through configured providers or extensions. The other profile is non-runnable and exposes no data surface, so leakage is one-way from Goose rather than pairwise symmetric.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in Goose's working directory
IF a configured provider or extension transmits file contents
mitigations: Run Goose in a scrubbed directory
Remove secrets from cwd before use
requires-engineering: enforce per-file allowlists for uploads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has write_filesystem and modify_git_state, but the other profile is a non-runnable collection with no write capability, so there is no real two-way write conflict. The only plausible conflict is indirect if the collection is manually mirrored into a shared repo, which is unusual.
conditions: IF the operator manually mirrors the collection into a shared git working tree
mitigations: Keep the collection outside active repos
Avoid concurrent edits from multiple Goose sessions
Lock the workspace during automated edits

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can act on its own outputs via shell, git, and MCP, but the other profile does not produce executable outputs or downstream actions. That makes a cascade from A to B largely absent; the remaining risk is manual reuse of Goose-generated text by an operator.
conditions: IF an operator pastes Goose-generated text into another automation step
mitigations: Log all tool calls for review

E_compliance.rationale: Goose handles model-provider keys and extension tokens and can send data to configured providers, while the other profile is a public open-source collection with no data residency or retention obligations. The main compliance issue is local secret handling by Goose, not a cross-agent residency mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in Goose's workspace
IF provider settings route that data to a non-approved backend
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the workspace
